assertions.description: Iterator.prototype.join is exposed as a function. Expected to FAIL before Chrome 153.
assertions.test: typeof Iterator !== 'undefined' && Iterator.prototype !== undefined && typeof Iterator.prototype.join === 'function'

assertions.description: An undefined separator defaults to a single comma, matching Array.prototype.join.
A non-undefined separator goes through ToString — an object with a toString method is accepted.
null and undefined elements contribute empty strings, matching Array.prototype.join.
Joining an already-exhausted or empty iterator returns the empty string (no throw — the difference from bare reduce).
Calling join with a non-object receiver throws a TypeError. Guarded on the method existing so an absent API fails instead of false-passing via its own TypeError.
assertions.test: typeof Iterator !== 'undefined' && Iterator.prototype !== undefined && typeof Iterator.prototype.join === 'function' && (() => { try { Iterator.prototype.join.call(42, ','); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()
